clue.text: Loudly sets off with crews having cool talent for trading

parts.note: a ship sails when it sets off
to man a vessel is to crew it, so crews gives this verb
hip is slang for fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: A boat crew sets off, apparently gifted at commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Salesmanship is the skill of persuading people to buy, a knack for commerce.

clue.text: Calls for problems around start of the week

indicators.note: the word for problems wraps around the day that begins the week

parts.note: arithmetic problems are sums
Monday, abbreviated, is the day that starts the working week

explanation.surface: Someone demands answers to troubles that arise as the week begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone is to call for them; summons is the third-person verb form.

clue.text: Seeds contributed to those French

parts.note: lent, as in lent a hand, means contributed
ils is French for they, those people

explanation.surface: Some seeds were given by a group of French people.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils are the edible seeds of a legume plant, cooked as pulses.

clue.text: Waterproof container with bit of suspicious smell English talk about

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: A sponge bag is the British name for a toiletry bag, lined to keep wet washing things in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge bag is a waterproof pouch for carrying toiletries such as a wet sponge.

clue.text: A duke and daughter happy to be consistent

parts.note: taken as written
up means in good spirits, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: A nobleman and his daughter are pleased to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: When a story adds up it makes sense, its details fitting together without contradiction.

clue.text: Ridiculous huff led, in part, to mix up

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of ridiculous, all of huff and the start of led

explanation.definitionFit: To shuffle cards or papers is to jumble them, mixing their order.

clue.text: Carpathian is going to resolve hostility

will means determination or resolve

explanation.surface: The setter announces a plan to settle a feud.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so Carpathian is the first person.

clue.text: One RBS manager's horribly awkward

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
the word without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A bank boss at the Royal Bank of Scotland has made a cringeworthy mess.
explanation.walkthrough: RBS is the Royal Bank of Scotland, a big UK bank whose bosses drew criticism after the 2008 crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Something embarrassing causes awkwardness and discomfort, an awkward situation.

clue.text: Encountered love embracing people in remembrance

indicators.note: the words for met and nil hug the word for people between them

parts.note: met means encountered
men, as in people generally
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake kept as a reminder, an object of remembrance.

clue.text: Duplicates game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: copies, exact twins of something
second meaning: a tennis or badminton game played two-a-side

explanation.definitionFit: Doubles are lookalike copies, and doubles is also the pairs format of tennis.

clue.text: Warden going to clubs for drinks

parts.note: screw is British slang for a prison officer
drivers are golf clubs used for long shots

explanation.surface: A prison guard heads off to nightclubs for a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests nightspots, but these are golf clubs.

clue.text: Bother group that's devoted

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
a ring is a group, such as a spy ring

explanation.surface: A troublesome gang that is wholly loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring describes deep affectionate devotion, worshipful love for someone.

clue.text: Seaside attraction visited by posh fellows looking more inflated

parts.note: a pier is a walkway out to sea at a resort
U is the old label for upper-class usage
F is fellow, doubled for the plural

explanation.definitionFit: Puffier means more swollen or bloated, the comparative of puffy.

clue.text: Son involved in fight returned with scrapes

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight

explanation.definitionFit: To rasp is to scrape with a rough file, so rasps means scrapes.

clue.text: Colleague of Spooner's strengthened cry

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of two words, so the two words here trade their first letters

parts.note: fed, as nourished and so strengthened
a bellow is a loud cry; said aloud its final w is silent, which is all Spooner's swap works on

explanation.surface: A shout that grew stronger, as the famous tongue-twisting Oxford don might say.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping initial sounds of words.

clue.text: Professor shares unopened gifts

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

parts.note: rations are allotted shares

explanation.surface: An academic hands out presents still in their wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shares' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Donations are gifts of money or goods to a cause.

clue.text: Tool for fixing small drum support with unlimited junk

parts.note: to drum one's fingers is to tap them
a leg supports a table

indicators.note: without limits means the outer letters of junk are lopped off

parts.note: its inner letters

explanation.definitionFit: A staple gun is a hand tool that drives staples to fasten material.

clue.text: In midst of song rotter finds paradise

indicators.note: the rotter sits in the middle of the word for song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter

explanation.surface: In the middle of an opera number, the villain finds bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the idealised pastoral land of Greek myth, a rural utopia.

clue.text: Tardis regularly placed in street for convenience

indicators.note: the chosen letters go inside the word for street

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one of Tardis

parts.note: its alternate letters

clue.text: Confused ostrich losing way in part of church

indicators.note: confused means the remaining letters are jumbled
losing means the letters for way are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
St, short for street, is a way

explanation.definitionFit: The choir is the area of a church where the singers sit, near the chancel.

clue.text: Many wearing charming item of clothing

indicators.note: the word for charming has the other word on it, round it like a garment

parts.note: cute means appealing or charming
a lot means many

explanation.surface: Lots of people are sporting a delightful garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A culotte is a divided skirt, a pair of wide-legged trousers cut like a skirt.

clue.text: Unconscious, having no lithium that's clear

indicators.note: having no means the lithium symbol is removed

parts.note: oblivious, unaware of one's surroundings

explanation.surface: Someone out cold without their lithium medication, as is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious means plain or evident, easy to see.

clue.text: Prompted college to replace verb in request by director

indicators.note: college's letter is to take the place of verb's letter

parts.note: to invite is to request someone's company
V is the grammar abbreviation for verb

explanation.surface: A college was urged to change a verb in a director's appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Incited means stirred up or urged on, prompted to act.

clue.text: Fear about to be suppressed by father

indicators.note: the word for about is held down inside the word for father

parts.note: dad
re means concerning or about

explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension.

parts.note: a valet is a manservant
IV is four in Roman numerals

clue.text: Try bit of dessert and enjoy — divine!

parts.note: its first letter
to like something is to enjoy it

explanation.surface: Taste a spoonful of pudding and savour it, it's heavenly!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' reads as praise for the pudding but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Godlike means like a god, so divine in nature.

clue.text: Excel with soldiers in the open air

parts.note: to outdo is to surpass or excel
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Shining alongside the troops out in the fresh air.

clue.text: Husband having brass header sculpted for those selling sewing things

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man with a brass head carved for the drapers' shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A haberdasher in Britain sells needles, thread and buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: Haberdashers are dealers in small sewing goods such as thread, ribbons and buttons.
